subject: SLA credit assessment and authorization — Cobalt Analytics incident
messages:
From: Tara Singh <tara.singh@cobalt-analytics.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@cobalt-analytics.com>, billing@cobalt-analytics.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Incident on 2027-03-08 — request for SLA credit eligibility

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the post-incident note earlier. We tracked a ~4 hour service degradation on 2027-03-08 (approx 02:10–06:25 UTC) that materially impacted our inference throughput for the Predict endpoint. Our SREs measured 42% request errors and high latencies during that window.

We need two things to complete our internal remediation and billing:
- confirmation of whether Cobalt is eligible for an SLA service credit for that outage window,
- the calculated credit amount or the formula you will use to compute it so we can reconcile with our finance team.

Can you confirm next steps and an expected timeline for a decision? If helpful, I attached our failure timeline.

Thanks —
Tara
Head of Platform, Cobalt Analytics

Attachment: cobalt-timeline-0308.txt (text)
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara.singh@cobalt-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incident on 2027-03-08 — request for SLA credit eligibility

Tara —

Appreciate the timeline and the details. Short answer: yes, this looks like it meets the eligibility criteria for an uptime-based credit under the SLA. I want to walk you through how we'll quantify it so there are no surprises.

High level next steps from our side (I expect to complete in ~48 hours):
1) Engineering will validate the incident window against our service metrics (prefix KV hits, failed request counts) — Marissa will run the calc.
2) We will compute the credit using the contractual formula (monthly uptime SLA and pro-rated credits).
3) Finance will prepare a credit memo and apply it to the next invoice or issue as a one-off offset depending on what you prefer.

Can you confirm you want the credit applied to your April invoice, or do you prefer a one-time account credit now?

I'll loop in Rishi for approval on the amount once Marissa posts the calculation.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Tara Singh <tara.singh@cobalt-analytics.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incident on 2027-03-08 — request for SLA credit eligibility

Thanks — I ran the numbers and attached the spreadsheet. Notes:
- Verified outage window from system metrics: 2027-03-08T02:08:00Z to 2027-03-08T06:25:00Z (4h17m).
- Monthly uptime for March (including incident) = 99.603% (after excluding scheduled maintenance windows).
- Per section 4.2 of our SLA, uptime < 99.7% qualifies for a credit.

Using the contract formula (pro-rated monthly service fee * % below SLA cap):
- Monthly committed fee (your contract): $48,000
- Credit percent per SLA table for 99.6% = 10% of monthly fee
- Calculated credit = $4,800

I attached slo_uptime_calc.xlsx which shows the step-by-step. If you have alternate contract language or a different seat/commit, call it out and I’ll recalc.

Attachment: slo_uptime_calc.xlsx (spreadsheet)

-Marissa
Senior Ops Analyst, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, billing@cobalt-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Approval: Cobalt Analytics SLA credit amount

Looping in finance: I reviewed Marissa's calc and supporting metrics. Approve issuing a $4,800 credit to Cobalt Analytics.

Operational notes for issuance:
- Apply as a one-time account credit against next invoice unless the customer explicitly requests immediate refund.
- Add a short credit memo referencing incident id RID-20270308-01 and HS-15432.
- Notify the customer and copy CS lead with the applied credit record.

Evelyn — can you draft the credit memo and send to billing@cobalt-analytics.com?

-Rishi
VP, Revenue Operations
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara.singh@cobalt-analytics.com>, billing@cobalt-analytics.com
Cc: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 16:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Credit memo — Cobalt Analytics (RID-20270308-01)

Tara / Cobalt billing team —

Per the approved SLA calculation, we've issued a one-time account credit of $4,800 to Cobalt Analytics for the incident on 2027-03-08 (Incident RID-20270308-01). Details:

- Credit amount: $4,800
- Applied to account: Cobalt Analytics (CBLT-2026-07)
- Reference: RID-20270308-01 / HS-15432
- Method: Account credit applied to next invoice (April 2027). If you'd prefer an immediate refund, reply and we'll route to finance.

Attached: credit_memo_template.pdf (credit memo)

Next steps on our side:
- I'll update the HubSpot ticket (HS-15432) with the memo and mark as resolved.
- Marissa / Engineering will close the incident audit and attach final metrics to the record.

Thanks for your patience — sorry again for the impact. Let me know if you want the memo emailed to a different contact.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Billing Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
